item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Okay, first things first. Good story; well-told. I like the fact that there's finally something resembling a sex-positive SCP in the database.

One thing I don't understand is why we gave it a body. In theory, they could have just kept 3101 locked away on the Windows computer with an air-gap and no network card. They could even have powered down said computer, putting 3101 to "sleep" so it would not be aware of any time passing. Isn't destroying or overwriting the D-class's consciousness so its body would become available at least as unethical as leaving 3101 in program-jail with only Windows manuals to read? We lock sapient entities up in solitary confinement all the time against their will. What makes this any different?

Gonna be honest, I was rooting for 3101 the whole time, to the point where I felt bad when they passed out! But this is a really strong departure from "The Foundation Is Cold." Such departures are entirely possible, of course, depending on cannon and especially when the Ethics Committee is involved. I just want to know the reason.

I refuse to believe they're somehow "more contained" in a human than in an off-network PC, or that their cooperation is strictly relevant when they're stuck in a powered-down computer with no network adapter.

Also, it's so not an infohazard. An infohazard is an SCP whose anomalous effects manifest as a direct result of knowing some information. A whole integer between six and seven which, when written, causes mathematics, and thus physics, to begin to break down. A letter which, when spoken, causes the listener's head to explode. A thing which we literally cannot remember or describe in any way, but which we discussed earlier and we're pretty sure was definitely not a sphere.

A computer program might be made of info, and it might present a hazard, but that doesn't make it an infohazard. Sauce.

item.content:encoded:
My only issue with is it that I don't think this counts as an infohazard.

How not? Its activity is triggered either at random or by people talking about it in text (which is an infohazard trait that's in other articles in the infohazard tag, admittedly, like 2521 for example):

+ show relevant excerpt
- collapse

SCP-3101: just type something and I'll come for you
SCP-3101: in multiple ways ;)

Agent Shaw: Interesting. And I am on MTF Lambda-12, yes. How did you learn that?

SCP-3101: i read a lot and i talk to people

Agent Shaw: Hmm. What was that about getting your attention? What do we say if we want you to show up?

SCP-3101: well uhhhhh you guys haven't given me a name yet but once you do I'll answer to it ;;

Agent Shaw: Let me ask.
Agent Shaw: It looks like the available slot was SCP-3101.

SCP-3101: Oh ok <3
SCP-3101: if you say that I'll come to the document I see it at and I'll talk

It functions as a textual infohazard. It just happens to also be sapient and claim that it won't creep on and/or edit any documents that get its attention, but obviously there's no way to guarantee it'll keep its word. If it weren't capable of conversation, it would look like a text-editing and text-searching anomaly that needs to get wiped out before it messes something up — which is arguably all it actually is, but the Ethics Committee didn't like that idea because it's intelligent.
